name: Paint Tree
description: You are given a tree with n vertexes and n points on a plane, no three points lie on one straight line. Your task is to paint the given tree on a plane, using the given points as vertexes. That is, you should correspond each vertex of the tree to exactly one point and each point should correspond to a vertex. If two vertexes of the tree are connected by an edge, then the corresponding points should have a segment painted between them. The segments that correspond to non-adjacent edges, should not have common points. The segments that correspond to adjacent edges should have exactly one common point.
input_specification: The first line contains an integer n ( 1 ≤ n ≤ 1500 ) — the number of vertexes on a tree (as well as the number of chosen points on the plane). Each of the next n - 1 lines contains two space-separated integers u i and v i ( 1 ≤ u i , v i ≤ n , u i ≠ v i ) — the numbers of tree vertexes connected by the i -th edge. Each of the next n lines contain two space-separated integers x i and y i ( - 10 9 ≤ x i , y i ≤ 10 9 ) — the coordinates of the i -th point on the plane. No three points lie on one straight line. It is guaranteed that under given constraints problem has a solution.
output_specification: Print n distinct space-separated integers from 1 to n : the i -th number must equal the number of the vertex to place at the i -th point (the points are numbered in the order, in which they are listed in the input). If there are several solutions, print any of them.
approach_summary: Precompute 2^k ancestor jumps up[u][k] and node depths in O(N log N). Compute LCA and path aggregates in O(log N) per query.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 196C — Paint Tree [146. Binary Lifting and LCA]
topic_editorial.summary: Binary lifting for lowest common ancestor and tree jumps.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Any ancestor jump of distance $K$ can be decomposed into powers of two $K = \sum 2^j$. Precomputing `up[u][k]` (the $2^k$-th ancestor of $u$) via `up[u][k] = up[up[u][k-1]][k-1]` allows any path or LCA to be answered in $O(\log N)$.
